card.name: Past-tense verbs after a subject
card.fires_on: Past-tense verbs such as caused, increased, gave or presented, right after a subject or a comma-set-off description. Most often the verb reporting an effect in drug-interaction or animal-study sentences.

modes.label: Interaction effect verb
modes.description: Verb like increased or caused after a named drug and its descriptive phrase, before the measured effect.
modes.example: Ketoconazole (400 mg daily), a selective and potent inhibitor of CYP3A4,<< increased>> tadalafil 20 mg single-d

modes.label: Study or finding verb
modes.description: Verb like caused or presented stating what a treatment or condition led to.
modes.example: treatment with COPIKTRA<< caused>> increased treatment-related mortality

modes.label: General narrative verb
modes.description: Past-tense verb in ordinary prose, such as gave, played or ran.
modes.example: G<<ave>> birth to froglets through the mouth.)

card.writes: No clear effect; it slightly favors short word endings and fragments over the continuation.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence names what something did, usually a past-tense verb like increased or caused.
